headline: ZIMBABWE'S ONLY LITHIUM PLANT FULL — NO ROOM FOR THIRD-PARTY ORE AS JANUARY 2027 EXPORT BAN CLOSES IN
snippet: Zimbabwe's sole lithium sulphate plant — operated by China's Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt at Prospect Lithium Zimbabwe — is fully allocated to its own concentrator output (roughly 400,000 tonnes per year) and has zero spare capacity to process third-party ore, a government official confirmed on July 17-18. The Mines Minister held the line on the January 2027 concentrate export ban deadline: miners who cannot process locally will face export prohibition in six months. The problem is structural: Zimbabwe exported approximately 1.128 million tonnes of spodumene concentrate in 2025, but the single operating plant cannot absorb even a fraction of that volume. Sinomine Resource Group's Bikita and China Yahua Group's Kamativi are building their own plants but are unlikely to be ready before the deadline. For junior mining investors this story highlights the supply chain disruption risk embedded in resource-nationalist vertical integration mandates — and raises a real question about whether Zimbabwe's spodumene export volume will simply fall off a cliff in Q1 2027 if processing capacity does not materialize, adding an unexpected tightness signal to the lithium market.

headline: SILVER SINKS TO $55 DESPITE SIXTH STRAIGHT ANNUAL DEFICIT — 762 MILLION OZ CUMULATIVE DRAWDOWN BURIED UNDER FED FEAR
snippet: Silver traded at approximately $54-55 per ounce on July 17, 2026 — while the Silver Institute's World Silver Survey confirmed the sixth consecutive structural supply deficit: 46.3 million ounces in 2026, up from 40.3 million in 2025, bringing the estimated cumulative six-year drawdown on above-ground stocks to 762 million ounces. The disconnect between record physical depletion and a declining spot price is a function of silver's structural supply inelasticity — approximately 74% of silver is produced as a byproduct of copper, lead, and zinc mining, meaning supply responds to those metals' economics rather than silver's own price signal. Industrial demand (photovoltaics, EVs, AI data-centre build-out, and semiconductors) represents 58% of total consumption and is growing faster than byproduct supply can match. The near-term headwind is the Fed: US-Iran war risk pushing oil above $84/bbl has revived rate-hike expectations that are keeping the dollar firm and precious metals under pressure. J.P. Morgan still forecasts silver averaging $81/oz for 2026 and HSBC has it at $75/oz — implying 36-47% upside from current levels. For retail investors in silver mining stocks, the six-consecutive-deficit frame is the strongest fundamental argument for the sector that exists in any commodity market right now.

headline: COPPER TICKS BACK ABOVE $6.17 AS IRAN CEASEFIRE TALK EASES DEMAND FEARS; CHILE STORM SUPPLY GAP HOLDS THE FLOOR
snippet: Copper futures edged higher on July 18 as diplomatic signals around a possible US-Iran ceasefire softened the demand-destruction fears that have weighed on base metals since the conflict escalated. Comex copper found a dual support base: Chile's monster winter storm — which stalled operations at Codelco's Andina and El Teniente, Antofagasta's Los Pelambres, and Anglo American's operations last week — has left physical supply tighter than futures markets initially priced. Chile's government simultaneously cut its 2026 economic growth forecast to 1.8% while raising its copper price assumption to $5.90/lb, an implicit acknowledgment that supply disruption risk is structurally underpriced. Any credible Iran de-escalation would be meaningfully positive for copper demand, while the Chile storm aftermath and Antofagasta's H1 production miss of 9.5% year-on-year keep the supply side supportive. Copper has given up roughly 7% from June highs and analysts at Macquarie and Canaccord view the current range as an accumulation zone rather than the start of a bear move.

headline: LI-FT POWER FIRES UP 163 HOLES AND 38,970m AT QUÉBEC'S ADINA-GALINÉE — ONE OF CANADA'S LARGEST LITHIUM DRILL PROGRAMS (TSXV:LIFT)
snippet: Li-FT Power Ltd. (TSXV: LIFT; ASX: LFT) announced on July 17 the commencement of drilling at the Adina-Galinée Lithium Project in Québec — one of the largest hard-rock lithium exploration programs in Canada this cycle, targeting 163 diamond drill holes over 38,970 metres. The AGLP was assembled through Li-FT's 2026 acquisition of Winsome Resources Limited and agreements with Azimut Exploration Inc. and SOQUEM Inc., consolidating a large spodumene pegmatite complex in the James Bay lithium corridor of northern Québec — the same region that hosts Patriot Battery Metals' Corvette deposit. The 2026 program aims to advance a mineral resource estimate across the full claim block, with parallel exploration also underway at the Cancet, Tilly, Nottaway, and Sirmac-Clapier properties. The program launch signals that well-funded juniors in Tier 1 Canadian jurisdictions are pressing forward on resource definition even at depressed lithium carbonate prices — betting the recovery underway at MinRes's Bald Hill (first production in July 2026 after 18-month care and maintenance) and Core Lithium's Finniss (recommissioning September 2026) is a leading indicator of the next supply tightness cycle.

headline: POWER METALLIC DRILLS 36.42m OF 2.83% CuEq AT NEW LION — ALL WINTER ASSAYS IN, MAIDEN MRE DUE END OF JULY (TSXV:PNPN)
source_name: PR Newswire / Power Metallic Mines Inc.
snippet: Power Metallic Mines (TSXV: PNPN; OTCQB: PNPNF) released final assay results from its Winter 2026 drill program at the New Lion project on July 15, completing the dataset to support the initial NI 43-101 Mineral Resource Estimate (MRE) on the Lion deposit. Headline hole 26-116 intersected 36.42 metres at 2.83% CuEqRec1 from 75 metres depth, including semi-massive sulphide over 6.00 metres at 12.38% CuEqRec1. The Winter 2026 program as a whole has been remarkably consistent: other infill holes returned 13.30 metres at 3.98% CuEq, 5.26 metres at 8.45% CuEq, 27.1 metres at 2.17% CuEq, and the season's standout of 22 metres at 11.46% CuEq — its second-best intersection ever. With all Winter 2026 assays now in hand, the MRE on both Lion and the adjacent Nisk deposit is scheduled for completion and reporting by month-end, followed immediately by a Preliminary Economic Assessment. High-grade near-surface copper on the TSXV with an imminent resource milestone and consistent hole-by-hole delivery marks Power Metallic as one of the more credible copper discovery stories in the junior space right now.

headline: USA RARE EARTH TIGHTENS SVRE MERGER — OFFTAKE DEAL MUST BE IRONCLAD BEFORE BRASIL VERDE ACQUISITION CLOSES (Nasdaq:USAR)
snippet: USA Rare Earth, Inc. (Nasdaq: USAR) entered Amendment No. 1 to its Merger Agreement with SVRE Holdings Ltd. on July 16, adding a new closing condition requiring the April 20 offtake agreement to be fully effective and irrevocably in force at closing — including satisfaction of certain conditions precedent, the lapse of SV Management Switzerland's unilateral termination right, and ongoing validity of the offtake arrangement. USAR's pending deal would give it control of Serra Verde Rare Earths Ltd., a Brazilian ionic clay rare earth project carrying high concentrations of neodymium and praseodymium (NdPr) critical for EV permanent magnets. The amendment tightens protections around the commercial underpinning of the merger — specifically ensuring USAR has locked-in offtake before crossing the finish line on a deal that includes significant CHIPS Act financing and debt complexity. USAR shares have fallen more than 20% since June 30 despite surging 81% in H1 2026, suggesting markets view the added legal complexity as deal execution risk. The manoeuvre illustrates the legal sophistication now required to close cross-border rare earth deals involving Brazilian resources as US-China competition in critical mineral supply chains intensifies.

headline: FRONTIER NUCLEAR LAUNCHES 120-HOLE, 36,000m URANIUM DRILL IN WYOMING'S POWDER RIVER BASIN — MRE TARGET: EARLY 2027 (Nasdaq:FNUC)
source_name: GlobeNewswire / Frontier Nuclear and Minerals Inc.
snippet: Frontier Nuclear and Minerals Inc. (Nasdaq: FNUC) launched its 2026 exploration drill program at the 100%-owned Pine Ridge uranium project in Wyoming's Powder River Basin on July 14, targeting approximately 120 holes over 36,000 metres from July 2026 into early 2027. The program objective is to define roll-front deposits and produce a maiden NI 43-101 Mineral Resource Estimate by early 2027. Last year's inaugural 2025 drill confirmed widespread uranium mineralization across multiple sandstone packages and identified at least 25 mineralized roll fronts — the structural confidence needed to scale up significantly. Frontier also expanded the Pine Ridge claim block by 54 federal mining claims (approximately 854 acres) ahead of the launch. Uranium spot is trading near $85.45/lb — supported by a structural supply deficit, US government reinstatement of uranium on the USGS Critical Minerals List, $80 billion in committed Westinghouse AP1000 reactor investment, and hyperscaler nuclear offtake agreements from major tech companies. A maiden Wyoming ISR resource from Frontier would land in one of the most constructive US domestic uranium market environments in decades, at a time when the US produces virtually none of its own primary supply.

headline: BRAZIL CRACKS URANIUM OPEN TO PRIVATE CAPITAL — STATE FIRM INB KEEPS 20% FLOOR AS DECADES-LONG MONOPOLY ENDS
snippet: Brazil circulated a draft regulation on July 13 that would end the decades-long monopoly of state-owned Nuclear Industries of Brazil (INB) over the country's nuclear fuel cycle, allowing INB to partner with private companies to mine, process, industrialize, and sell uranium and other nuclear minerals. The structure requires the private partner to fund 100% of project investment costs and allows the private company to hold a controlling stake if the value of INB's contributed mining assets falls short of total capital required — effectively subordinating state capital to private risk capital. INB would retain a minimum 20% equity position in each venture. Brazil holds the world's sixth-largest uranium reserves — an estimated 276,700 tonnes at Caetité in Bahia and deposits in Minas Gerais — almost entirely undeveloped relative to global peers. The draft is under review at the Chief of Staff's office and the Mines and Energy Ministry; changes may be made before finalization. If enacted, it would be the most significant opening of Brazil's nuclear resource sector since 1988 and could attract meaningful foreign and domestic capital to a resource endowment that has historically been locked away from the international market. It also arrives exactly when uranium demand — driven by AI data-centre base-load power and the global nuclear renaissance — is at its strongest in two decades.

headline: ALTIUS MINERALS RAISES C$181.5M TO BANKROLL 2026 ROYALTY BLITZ — LITHIUM, RENEWABLES AND COAL ROYALTIES ALL ACQUIRED THIS YEAR (TSX:ALS)
snippet: Altius Minerals Corporation (TSX: ALS; OTCQX: ATUSF) announced a C$181.5 million bought deal on July 14, priced at C$60.50 per share with National Bank Financial, Scotia Capital, and TD Securities — plus an overallotment option that could push total gross proceeds to approximately C$209 million. Shares dropped 14.1% on the dilution announcement. Proceeds will replenish the balance sheet after a significant 2026 acquisition run that has made Altius the most active royalty buyer in the critical minerals space: in March, it acquired Lithium Royalty Corp and its 38 royalties on lithium and critical mineral properties for approximately $140 million in cash and shares; in June, it committed US$73 million into the 311 MW Coles Wind royalty in Illinois; and on July 10, it agreed to acquire Northampton Capital's minority interest in Altius Renewable Royalties, lifting its effective stake in Great Bay Renewables from 29% to 50%. Altius is methodically assembling a diversified royalty book across battery metals, energy transition minerals, and renewable energy — a strategy that mirrors Franco-Nevada and Wheaton's model in precious metals but applied to the next commodity cycle. Closing is expected July 21, 2026.

headline: ALL 18 RARE EARTH ELEMENTS RISE IN JULY — GERMANIUM +27.8%, DYSPROSIUM +25.4%; PROJECT VAULT LAUNCHES $10B US RESERVE
snippet: All 18 rare earth elements tracked by industry analysts rose in price in July 2026, with germanium leading at a 27.8% domestic price surge and dysprosium — critical for EV and wind turbine permanent magnets — gaining 25.4%, with an average basket gain of 16.7% for the month. The structural driver is a second consecutive year of supply deficit against EV, wind turbine, and AI infrastructure demand, compounded by China's strategic control over approximately 80% of global rare earth processing and ongoing export restriction risk. On the policy side, the Trump administration's Project Vault — a direct response to Chinese export controls — established a US Strategic Critical Minerals Reserve funded by $10 billion in Export-Import Bank financing and $2 billion in private capital, targeting rare earth stockpiling ahead of anticipated further restrictions from Beijing. US-listed rare earth stocks surged 81% in H1 2026, led by USA Rare Earth (USAR) and MP Materials, though both have pulled back more than 20% from June 30 highs as deal complexity and profit-taking weighed. Analysts at Benchmark Mineral Intelligence assess another round of Chinese rare earth export restrictions as more likely than not before year-end — which would be a significant catalyst for North American and Australian rare earth developers.

headline: GOLD SWOT: MINERS 'TEEING UP FOR FURTHER GROWTH' — RECORD-WIDE GOLD-EQUITY DISCOUNT ECHOES H2 2023 BUY SETUP (GoldSeek)
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly SWOT analysis of gold mining stocks argues that senior and mid-tier miners — sitting 20-40% below 52-week highs even as gold holds above $4,000 — are exhibiting technical and fundamental setups that have historically preceded major re-rating moves relative to the metal. The gold-equity discount is identified as the key Strength: every dollar of gold above $3,500 drops to bottom-line margins miners have never seen, yet stock prices reflect fear rather than fundamentals, with GDX closing near 71.32 and the median precious metals stock 40% below its 52-week high as of mid-July. Weaknesses include persistent cost inflation and the heavy H2 production-weighting that leaves full-year guidance exposed to weather or operational disruption before year-end. Opportunities: the institutional consensus (JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs) for gold above $4,000 year-end is intact; any Iran ceasefire or Fed pivot could simultaneously re-price metal and compress the equity discount hard and fast. Threat: a genuine recession triggered by Middle East energy-price shock could undercut industrial metals sentiment and weigh on the broader sector. GoldSeek's conclusion: the setup resembles H2 2023, when a sector that looked structurally impaired at lower gold prices subsequently outperformed the metal by approximately 40% over the following 12 months.
